papers.title: Engineering Geological Assessment and Landslide Hazard Zonation Using the Slope Stability Susceptibility Evaluation Parameter Method Around Gidole Town, Southern Ethiopia
papers.summary: Gidole Town and its surrounding areas have experienced repeated landslide events that have damaged roads, farmland, and settlements, yet detailed engineering geological investigations and quantitative hazard assessments remain limited. This study investigates the engineering geological factors controlling slope instability and develops a landslide hazard zonation map using the Slope Stability Susceptibility Evaluation Parameter (SSEP) method. The research integrates detailed geological and geomorphological mapping, structural discontinuity measurements, landslide inventory mapping, laboratory testing of representative soil samples, and Geographic Information System (GIS)-based spatial analysis. The results show that highly weathered basalt, unconsolidated colluvial deposits, steep slopes, groundwater seepage, and intense seasonal rainfall are the primary controls on landslide occurrence in the study area. The hazard zonation model classified 67.7% of the area as high hazard, 29.0% as moderate hazard, and 3.4% as low hazard. Model validation using the mapped landslide inventory indicated that approximately 74% of documented landslides fall within the predicted high-hazard zones, demonstrating the robustness and reliability of the SSEP approach. The resulting hazard map provides a scientific basis for land-use planning, infrastructure development, slope stabilization, and disaster risk reduction in southern Ethiopia. The findings further demonstrate that the SSEP method is an effective and practical tool for landslide hazard assessment in data-constrained mountainous regions.

papers.title: An internally consistent framework for calculating cascading probabilistic earthquake risk and its application to a case study in New Zealand
papers.source: Natural hazards and earth system sciences
papers.summary: Abstract. Quantifying the combined effects of earthquakes and their cascading hazards is essential for realistic risk assessment, yet such approaches remain limited in practice. Dynamic frameworks that explicitly correlate hazard intensities and their uncertainties across cascading perils provide more consistent and physically plausible impact estimates, offering greater value for resilience planning and risk management. This study introduces a probabilistic risk assessment framework that integrates ground shaking, tsunami inundation, liquefaction, landslides, and their combined impacts into a unified modelling approach. The framework employs a fully correlated Monte Carlo–based hazard and damage model, ensuring that secondary perils and their effects on assets are conditionally linked to the triggering ground motions. This dynamic correlation maximises the representation of realistic damage scenarios. The framework was tested in Napier, a city of 65,000 inhabitants situated directly above the Hikurangi Subduction Zone (HSZ), New Zealand’s largest earthquake source with an estimated maximum credible magnitude of about Mw9.1. A 100,000-year stochastic catalogue of ruptures was generated and applied to ~30,000 residential buildings, with ground shaking, tsunami inundation, liquefaction severity, and landslide runouts explicitly modelled. Results include damage state and damage ratio metrics for individual and combined perils. Earthquake shaking and liquefaction emerge as the dominant drivers of risk, followed by tsunami, lateral spreading, and landslides. These findings demonstrate the importance of capturing interdependent hazards in earthquake risk analysis. The framework provides decision makers, urban planners, and the (re)insurance sector with actionable metrics to guide resilience investments, refine underwriting, and minimise losses from cascading hazard events.

papers.title: Debris flow susceptibility assessment along the G55 expressway in Guangdong Province, China
papers.summary: Western Guangdong Province in China is frequently affected by intense rainfall and related geological hazards, yet studies on debris flow disasters in this area remain limited. In June 2025, four consecutive debris flow events occurred along the Lianzhou-Sanshui section of the G55 Erenhot-Guangzhou Expressway, attracting significant attention. To better understand the spatial distribution and controlling factors of these hazards, this study conducted a debris flow susceptibility assessment for this section. Based on regional topographic, meteorological, and geological conditions, combined with historical disaster data, an evaluation index system and database were established. Four machine learning algorithms, Back Propagation Neural Network (BPNN), Random Forest (RF), Support Vector Machine (SVM), and Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), were applied and systematically compared. Algorithm performance was assessed using 3-fold spatially independent validation. Among the tested algorithms, XGBoost achieved the best predictive performance, with an accuracy of 0.923, recall of 0.879, F1-score of 0.794, and ROC-AUC of 0.927. The debris flow susceptibility was classified into low, medium, and high levels. Medium and high susceptibility areas exhibited clear spatial clustering, mainly in the northern section of the expressway, while the southern section showed generally low susceptibility. Debris flows along the expressway were primarily triggered by shallow surface collapses and landslides that formed cascading hazard chains, while the slipperiness of surface weathering products showed an observed association with debris-flow occurrence and may represent a potential conditioning factor. These findings provide a scientific basis for debris flow risk identification and mitigation and offer insights for improving susceptibility assessment methodologies.

papers.title: Hyperspectral Imaging and Deep Learning for Disaster Monitoring Systems
papers.summary: As natural disasters become more frequent and severe, there's a growing need for an advanced monitoring system that can detect them early and assess their impact accurately. Hyperspectral imaging (HSI) collects detailed spectral data across hundreds of adjacent bands. This makes it a powerful tool for finding and studying disasters like wildfires, floods, landslides, and oil spills. This chapter examines the integration of deep learning models with remote sensing data to create dependable and scalable framework for disaster monitoring. The study employs data from NASA's AVRIS and the Italian Space Agency's PRISMA missions to assess essential preprocessing techniques, such as noise elimination and dimensionality reduction. This paper presents a comparative analysis of deep learning architectures focusing on 3D convolutional neural networks (3D CNNs) for efficient spatial– spectral extraction and hybrid CNN–RNN models for spectral analysis. Moreover, segmentation models such as U-Net are evaluated for accurate spatial separation. To ensure the system's robustness and transferability for real-time application, the developed techniques were tested using more accessible multispectral imagery. This paper aims to use the power of spectral resolution and advanced artificial intelligence to make disaster management systems that are smart, strong, and quick to respond.

papers.title: Landslide Susceptibility Mapping for Railway Slopes Using Comparative Models and InSAR-Based Validation
papers.summary: Abstract We evaluated landslide susceptibility along the Carajás Railway in Brazil using five approaches: Random Forest, Extreme Gradient Boosting, Multilayer Perceptron, Support Vector Machine, and Weight of Evidence. The models integrated an inventory of 148 landslide events with geomorphological, hydrological, and land-use conditioning factors. We assessed predictive performance using receiver operating characteristic curves and the area under the curve. Random Forest performed best (0.859), followed by Extreme Gradient Boosting (0.850), Multilayer Perceptron (0.687), Weight of Evidence (0.669), and Support Vector Machine (0.459). We independently evaluated susceptibility predictions using ground-deformation time series derived from Sentinel-1 interferometric synthetic aperture radar data processed with the Small Baseline Subset approach. Deformation rates increased progressively across susceptibility classes, with the highest magnitudes concentrated in areas classified as highly susceptible. Random Forest and Extreme Gradient Boosting showed the strongest agreement between susceptibility patterns and observed deformation. The results indicated that interferometric deformation provided an independent physical assessment of susceptibility predictions and strengthened the interpretation of model outputs. The integrated approach improved the reliability of susceptibility assessment and supported risk-informed management of railway slopes.

papers.title: Preliminary Hypothesis About the Polygonal Features Discovered in a Middle Miocene Deep-Sea Sediment Sequence (Kawabata Fm., Hokkaido, Japan)
papers.summary: Numerous landslides occurred in the region of Atsuma (Hokkaido, Japan) as a result of the 2018 Hokkaido Eastern Iburi Earthquake. Despite their devastating consequences, the emergence of mass movements has provided a unique opportunity to gain insight into specific chapters of Earth’s history by exposing new natural outcrops and revealing rock strata, including the Middle Miocene Kawabata Formation. The formation primarily comprises sedimentary rocks that reflect various deep-sea environments, especially the continental slope and basin plain of a foreland basin. For this reason, an exposed bedding plane consisting of polygonal features, recently (September 2022) discovered in an outcrop formed at the scarp of a landslide, has aroused interest. Mud cracks or desiccation marks often form in the tidal zone due to exposure to the subaerial environment but not in the aforementioned deep-sea facies. An additional series of evidence of subaerial exposure, with potential wet and dry cycles in a near-shore/coastal environment, was revealed, such as limonite grain coatings and hypocoatings, as well as biotite exfoliation. Based on this evidence, a putative new Middle Miocene facies and a potential new stratigraphic member was proposed in the Kawabata Formation.

papers.title: InSAR observations from multiple tracks reveal rainfall modulation of post-failure reactivation of the Xiongwadashan landslide
papers.summary: Large mountain landslides may remain active after major movement, yet the migration of dominant deformation zones, internal post-failure partitioning, and rainfall modulation remain insufficiently understood. We investigate the Xiongwadashan (XW) landslide on the northeastern Tibetan Plateau using Sentinel-1 LOS observations from selected pre- and post-event periods between 2017 and 2025, terrain-constrained three-dimensional displacement estimates for 2022–2024, CHIRPS rainfall data, and field observations. Before the September 2018 event, deformation was concentrated mainly in the middle–lower slope. After failure, the dominant deformation zone shifted to the middle–upper slope and later extended partially downslope toward the middle slope. Movement was dominated by horizontal, near-downslope displacement, with a peak cumulative east–west displacement of ~ 210 mm at XW1-3. Integrated LOS deformation, three-dimensional displacement, time series, and geomorphic evidence delineated high-deformation, transitional, and low-deformation kinematic zones. The high-deformation zone showed stronger displacement increases following concentrated rainfall, while deformation persisted during relatively low-rainfall periods. These results indicate that rainfall mainly modulated stage-wise acceleration rather than controlling long-term activity, and demonstrate the value of integrating temporal deformation-zone migration with internal kinematic zonation for post-failure landslide monitoring.

papers.title: Integrating Social Innovation and Geoinformatics for Community-Based Disaster Risk Reduction: A Sandbox Approach in Mueang Tak District, Thailand
papers.summary: Background and Objectives: Natural disasters, particularly landslides, floods, and droughts, pose increasing threats to the socio-economic stability and environmental security of communities in Mueang Tak District, Tak Province, Thailand. Conventional top-down disaster management strategies often suffer from a critical data-action gap in which advanced spatial technologies and risk information are not effectively translated into locally actionable practices. To address this challenge, this study aimed to integrate social innovation with geoinformatics technology to strengthen community-based disaster risk reduction. The specific objectives were to analyze natural disaster risk areas using Geographic Information Systems (GIS) and Remote Sensing (RS), investigate community-based social innovation needs, and develop and evaluate “Sandbox Innovation Areas” for landslide, flood, and drought management. Methodology: The study employed an integrated research design structured into four phases: spatial risk assessment, community survey, participatory sandbox development, and evaluation. Spatial data were processed using Google Earth Engine (GEE) and GIS to identify priority risk areas. Social data were collected from 462 residents using stratified multistage cluster random sampling across landslide-prone, flood-prone, and drought-prone areas to assess existing practices and innovation needs. Spatial and social findings were integrated to guide the selection of three pilot sandbox areas and the design of capacity-building activities for Community Innovators. The sandbox process included participatory GIS, field validation, co-creation of community risk maps, and evaluation of perceived knowledge gain and stakeholder opinions. papers.title: Enhancing Disaster Resilience in the Himalayan Region through AI and Emerging Technologies
papers.summary: The Himalayan region is among the most disaster-prone areas globally, characterized by complicated geomorphology, steep gradients along with an active tectonic environment. The area is highly prone to numerous natural hazards such as earthquakes, flooding, landslides, glacial lake outburst floods, avalanches, cloudburst, and forest fires. The rising frequency and severity of these hazards, influenced by climate change and anthropogenic pressures, underscore the urgent need for effective disaster prediction, risk assessment, and mitigation frameworks, specifically adapted to the sensitive ecosystem. This chapter presents a narrative review of recent advances in geoAI and investigates the recent integration of AI-driven models, such as deep learning, machine learning and geospatial analytics, remote sensing, and GIS for forecasting complex natural hazards with higher accuracy. This article provides an in-depth examination of natural hazards in the context of the Indian Himalayas, including their causes, spatial–temporal distributions, and socio-environmental impacts on the region. Based on peer-reviewed studies as well as case studies in practice, this study shows that the Indian Himalayan Region (IHR) is becoming a paradigm shift in disaster risk reduction based on several emerging technologies. Emerging technologies and methods are enhancing and improving modeling, forecasting, and overall hazard prediction in multi-hazard modeling (hydrological modeling, flood warnings, and GLOFs warnings). The use of sophisticated machine-learning (ML) frameworks (deep learning models including CNN, U-Net, Random Forest, and XGBoost models) as well as AI-geospatial and model integrations are revolutionizing hazard prediction and multi-hazard modeling processes. papers.title: Multisource Information-Based Social Event Detection Using Integrated Deep Neural Architectures and Hybrid Text Representation
papers.summary: Event detection is crucial for timely crisis response, public safety, and combating misinformation by extracting critical signals from real-time social data. The user-generated content on social media platforms has created a critical need for intelligent systems capable of accurately detecting and classifying real-world events across diverse domains. This paper presents a fusion-driven framework for social event detection, leveraging textual data from diverse social media sources and a suite of deep neural architectures to achieve state-of-the-art performance in classifying diverse event categories from noisy, unstructured social media streams. The proposed system collects information from heterogeneous domains, including medical conditions, natural disasters, and sports events, to improve both feature richness and contextual awareness. Our method applies a hybridized deep learning strategy, specifically a customized layered CNN+LSTM architecture. This fusion enables the model to learn spatial and temporal dependencies simultaneously, thus enhancing classification performance. To benchmark effectiveness, we evaluated standalone architectures including CNN, RNN, LSTM, BiLSTM, and BiRNN. Among individual models, LSTM and BiLSTM yielded the top performance, achieving up to 95.3% and 95.8% precision, 95.5% and 96.1% recall, 95.4% and 95.9% accuracy, 95.4% and 96.0% F1-score, 95.6% and 96.2% F1.5, and 95.5% and 96.1% F2-scores, respectively. However, these models still showed variability across event types due to limited contextual generalization from a single-layered perspective. In contrast, the proposed fused CNN and LSTM model recorded promising performance with superior F1-scores on 14 independent classes, achieving 100% on Acne, Earthquake, Landslide, Ringworm, and Vitiligo, 99% on Depression, 98% on Badminton and Tennis, 97% on Cricket, and 96% on FIFA (2022). These results demonstrate the model’s robustness across both high- and low-frequency classes, as well as

papers.title: A Comprehensive Review on Statistical and Artificial Intelligence Techniques for Landslide Analysis
papers.summary: Landslides are one of the most devastating phenomena and account for nearly 4.5% of all natural hazards worldwide. The disruption caused by landslides is on the rise globally due to climate change and extreme weather events. The increment in human population has led to rapid expansion in infrastructural development, which often requires deforestation and natural slope tempering through excavation leading to slope failures. The destabilized slopes, coupled with triggering factors such as rainfall or earthquake, pose a significant threat of landslides, especially to communities residing in landslide-prone regions. A substantial number of these events occurred in the Himalayan region. The fragile Himalayan ecosystem is witnessing tremendous economic growth without manifesting a genuine concern for the environment. The landslide risk studies have picked up pace in recent decades owing to recent development of predictive studies using GIS and artificial intelligence techniques. This study aims to review the evolution of landslide susceptibility, vulnerability, and risk analysis studies with focus on recent techniques based on machine learning and ensemble modeling.

papers.source: International Journal of Advanced Research in Science Communication and Technology
authors: Pranav Gojare, Vedant Nemade, Arshiya Shaikh
papers.summary: Collapsed buildings, mine roofs and landslides trap people under heavy debris, and their chances of survival fall as time passes. Finding the exact position of a victim is the slowest and riskiest part of collapsed structure search and rescue (CSSR), especially in rural and mining-affected areas where modern equipment, light and stable ground are not available. This paper studies an Advance Body Detection System (ABDS) that sends 1.5 GHz radio-frequency (RF) waves into the debris and uses a low-cost thermal camera to confirm the heat of a human body. The architecture, the RF chain (antenna, VCO, LNA, mixer and analog-to-digital detector), the processing unit and a decision logic that cross-references both sensors are explained with block diagrams, a signal-processing chain and a flowchart, and basic calculations for the RF module and the thermal camera are given. The study, based on recent literature (2020 onwards), shows that RF waves can pass through non-metallic debris and sense the small movement of a hidden person, while a thermal camera detects body heat only at the surface; using both together gives more confident detection than either alone. The main limitations are unwanted reflections from debris, metal and moisture, limited penetration depth, radio-frequency regulations and the need for field trials. No experiments were carried out; calculated values are typical values for explanation

papers.title: Upper bound solution under rainfall-earthquake coupling for curvilinear shallow landslides considering progressive failure mechanism
papers.source: International Conference on Advances in Energy and Environmental Engineering (AEEE)
papers.summary: The shallow landslides are mostly triggered by rainfall and earthquakes. Shallow slopes usually exhibit curved profiles, and obvious multi-stage characteristics are showed in their progressive failure process due to the coupling effect of rainfall and earthquake. Based on the improved upper bound method of limit analysis theory, the stability of curved shallow slopes was analyzed under different coupling conditions of rainfall and earthquakes. A logarithmic spiral sliding surface was proposed for the typical terrain features of steep terrain, and pseudo static seismic effects were corrected to use acceleration amplification coefficients. By the strength and pore water pressure power, the expression was derived for the evolution of the wetting front. Then the energy balance equation was established, four stages of progressive failure mechanisms were revealed. The critical wetting front depth and sliding body length were solved by constructing an allowable velocity field and establishing a variational optimization framework based upon the Euler Lagrange equation. The stability influence of shallow slopes was analyzed depended on effective cohesion, static soil pressure coefficient, and maximum central slope angle. The results indicated that effective cohesion played a key controlling role in the depth of the critical wetting front. The sliding scale was mostly impacted on the static soil pressure coefficient. The maximum central slope angle does not decouple the infiltration process excepted with mainly adjusts the sliding range. These results are good with agree with the values of finite elements method. This study provides a scientific basis for the stability analysis and disaster prevention of curved slopes in mountainous areas.

papers.title: From Fragmented Plans to a Public Regulatory Knowledge Infrastructure: Harmonizing Flood and Landslide Risk Planning in the Central Apennine River Basin District, Italy
papers.summary: Italy’s transition to river basin district governance within the framework of Directive 2000/60/EC unified institutional responsibilities while leaving existing flood and landslide plans in force. District authorities therefore had to integrate instruments with different knowledge bases, classifications and land-use rules. This article examines the integration of nine Hydrogeological Setting Plans (PAIs) into two coordinated plans for the Central Apennine district (42,275 km2), adopted in final form in May 2026. Document analysis compared classifications, intervention conditions and assessment responsibilities, examining 175 public submissions and 118 first-round regional determinations. Geographic information system analysis quantified current classification correspondences and coverage: approximately 1860 km2 within the fluvial planning framework, including safeguard proposals, and 107,045 landslide phenomena occupying approximately 4970 km2. Initial flood transposition retained inherited boundaries, while landslide classification followed a common type–activity matrix. Regulatory comparisons identified conditional extensions of admissibility alongside more selective urban restructuring rules; the plans also established formal updating procedures. Institutional review connected technical choices with regulatory decisions, producing amendments while leaving some precautionary disagreements unresolved. The framework coordinated inherited knowledge without eliminating differences in detail or completeness. The article offers a procedural and regulatory reference for other authorities facing fragmented planning systems; implementation and risk-reduction outcomes require subsequent evaluation.

papers.title: A new method of landslide susceptibility assessment considering time-series InSAR surface deformation optimized non-landslide sample
papers.summary: Due to the severe casualties and property losses caused by landslides, carrying out landslide susceptibility assessment (LSA) has important theoretical value and practical significance. However, affected by factors such as non-landslide sample selection and prediction model parameter setting, the results of landslide susceptibility evaluation have a certain deviation from the actual situation. Based on the dual sampling strategy of non-landslide ‘low deformation’ and ‘buffer zone’, this paper uses the Northern Goshawk Optimization (NGO) algorithm to enhance the Random Forest (RF) model, and proposes an NGO-RF susceptibility evaluation method considering the optimization of non-landslide samples with time-series InSAR deformation. Taking Shuicheng District, Guizhou Province, China as the study area, the evaluation results are compared and analyzed with the RF, CatBoost and Multiple Linear Regression (MLR) models. The research results show that the evaluation results under the ‘low deformation’ sampling strategy are better than those under the ‘buffer zone’ strategy. In addition, the AUC-ROC value of the NGO-RF model under the ‘low deformation’ sampling strategy is 0.939, which is at least 2.3% higher than that of the RF, CatBoost and MLR models, presenting better evaluation performance. Meanwhile, different models also show certain differences in predicting the distribution of historical landslide points in the ‘low deformation’ and ‘buffer zone’ scenarios. The number of landslide points in the ‘very high’ risk zone predicted by the NGO-RF model increases from 86 to 136, while the number of landslide points in the ‘low’ risk zone decreases by 5, which significantly improves the accuracy and reliability of high-risk zones. This effectively verifies the effectiveness of the time-series InSAR deformation‑optimized non-landslide sample selection strategy, and can provide technical support for landslide disaster prediction, early warning, disaster prevention and mitigatio

papers.title: Remote Sensing-Based Detection and Prediction of Rainfall–Flood–Landslide Cascades in Eastern Kentucky
papers.source: Murray State's Digital Commons (Murray State University)
papers.summary: Eastern Kentucky is highly susceptible to flooding and landslides due to its steep terrain and narrow river valleys. Extreme rainfall can trigger flooding and destabilize hillslopes, creating cascading hazards that threaten communities and infrastructure. This study evaluates the relationships between natural and anthropogenic landscape characteristics and landslide susceptibility while comparing the predictive performance of statistical and machine learning approaches. Topographic, hydrologic, geologic, land cover, and anthropogenic variables were compiled from satellite-derived products and publicly available geospatial datasets for four major watersheds in Eastern Kentucky. The analysis covered August 2016 through August 2026, and a statewide landslide inventory was used to develop and evaluate three predictive models: binary logistic regression, Random Forest, and Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost). Model performance was assessed using receiver operating characteristic curves and the area under the curve (AUC). All three models demonstrated strong discriminatory performance, with AUC values of 0.9315 for logistic regression, 0.9596 for Random Forest, and 0.9495 for XGBoost. Random Forest achieved the highest AUC, although the improvement over logistic regression was marginal. These findings suggest that a comparatively interpretable statistical model can provide strong predictive performance without the additional complexity of more advanced machine learning approaches. This research provides a foundation for identifying landscape characteristics associated with landslide susceptibility in Eastern Kentucky and demonstrates the potential value of integrating geospatial data and predictive modeling to support regional natural hazard assessment.

papers.title: HUBUNGAN POLA PERSEBARAN PERMUKIMAN DENGAN TINGKAT KERAWANAN LONGSOR DI BUKIT GADO-GADO KECAMATAN PADANG SELATAN KOTA PADANG
papers.summary: The Gado-Gado Hill area in South Padang District is a landslide-prone protected zone. However, it has experienced rapid residential development driven by population growth and a scarcity of flat land. This study aims to analyze settlement distribution patterns and landslide susceptibility levels, as well as the relationship between the two, using a descriptive quantitative approach and GIS spatial analysis—specifically overlay, weighting, and scoring methods—based on parameters such as slope gradient, rainfall, soil type, land cover, geology, and landslide susceptibility in relation to settlements. The results indicate that settlements tend to cluster linearly along main roads across the lower to middle slopes; a significant area 95.996 hectares is classified as highly susceptible to landslides due to steep slopes, Brown Latosol soil, and an average rainfall of 424.15 mm/year. A significant correlation was found: the higher the settlement density in susceptible zones, the greater the disaster risk. These findings serve as a crucial basis for safe and sustainable spatial planning and disaster mitigation.

papers.title: Climate Change, Migration, and Social Cohesion among Young People: Evidence from DR Congo, Uganda, and Rwanda
papers.source: In Factis Pax: Journal of Peace Education and Social Justice
papers.summary: In the Democratic Republic of Congo, Uganda, and Rwanda, extreme weather events such as floods, droughts, and landslides disrupt communities and force people to migrate. These movements affect their social integration, educational trajectories, and participation in local communities. This study adopts a multi-site, mixed-methods approach to examine the impact of climate-induced displacement on youth vulnerability and social cohesion. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews, community observations, NGO reports, institutional records, local statistics, and school records. The study compares the experiences of displaced youth and host communities across the three countries, highlighting both challenges and strategies of resilience. Findings revealed the mechanisms through which migration affects social cohesion, the vulnerabilities of youth in displaced contexts, and the role of community networks in fostering resilience. The study contributes to the international debate on climate migration by providing empirical, intersectional evidence from a fragile region, offering recommendations for policymakers, local authorities, and development practitioners to enhance social cohesion and support youth affected by climate-induced displacement. The findings redefine climate migration as a multi-level governance issue with direct implications for social stability and youth development.

papers.title: From Reagan to Trump: regional development traps and the remaking of American electoral politics
papers.summary: This paper examines the territorial reconfiguration of American electoral politics since the 1980s, tracing the remaking of Republican support from Reagan’s 1984 landslide to Trump’s three presidential campaigns (2016, 2020, 2024). Drawing on panel data for every presidential election from 1984 to 2024 across 722 commuting zones, we test whether regional development traps, defined as enduring economic underperformance, explain both the shift from Democrats to Republicans and the Republicans’ internal realignment. Mundlak/Correlated Random Effects estimates show backlash is overwhelmingly driven by structural, not cyclical, decline. Short-term economic fluctuations do not predict Republican swing, while long-run territorial position does so decisively. Voters are not responding to recessions. They are registering alienation from an economic order that has failed their communities for a generation. Trump’s gains concentrated in places persistently left behind, whose peripheral position has become entrenched.

papers.title: Road Development in the Tropical Forests of Southeast Asia and the Pacific: A Systematic Review of Forest Loss, Ecological and Health Effects, and Mitigation
papers.summary: Background Road networks in Southeast Asian and Pacific tropical forests are expanding through highways, logging and plantation roads and unmapped access roads. This review synthesized primary evidence on road effects on forest loss, ecology and human health, and evaluated mitigation. Methods Scopus, PubMed and OpenAlex were searched on 7 October 2026 for English-language journal articles published from 2015 (PRISMA 2020). Reviewer 1 and Reviewer 2 independently screened 496 records (κ = 0.94) and assessed 80 full texts (κ = 0.80); the Adjudicator resolved disagreements. Studies were appraised with MMAT 2018, synthesized following SWiM and rated with GRADE-CERQual. Results Sixty-five studies were included, most from Malaysia, Indonesia and Thailand; 19 reported forest-loss, 47 ecological and six mitigation outcomes. Forest cover loss was greater nearer roads, at higher road density or length and after construction or completion in nine studies, and no study showed less loss (moderate confidence). Loss extended to 17.7 km with secondary roads in New Guinea (moderate). Structural edge effects reached 34 m at a logging road and 350 m at a highway, whereas soil effects stayed largely on the road surface (moderate). Reptiles or amphibians led roadkill in all seven surveys recording every vertebrate class, and mortality concentrated on short sections near water (moderate). Paved roads reduced crossing by elephants and gibbons and were linked to genetic differentiation in some taxa (moderate). Crossing structures were used by mammals and a large snake (moderate); measured effects rested on single spatial comparisons (very low). No study reported a human health outcome, and fire, landslides and water quality were unmeasured. Conclusions Roads act on these forests at two scales: kilometers for access-driven clearing, and tens to hundreds of meters for edge, mortality and barrier effects. Assessment boundaries and mitigation should match each mechanism’s scale, and mitigation

papers.title: Geomorphological Characteristics Based on Morphography, Morphometry, and Geomorphic Processes of the Silungkang Area, Sawahlunto City, West Sumatra
papers.summary: Geomorphology provides essential information on landscape evolution through the analysis of landforms, surface processes, and their controlling factors. This study was conducted in the Silungkang area and its surroundings, Sawahlunto City, West Sumatra, which lies within the Ombilin Basin, an intramontane basin interpreted as an oblique-rift to pull-apart basin associated with the Sumatra Fault System. The objective of this research is to identify and classify the geomorphology of the study area through morphographic, morphometric, and geomorphic-process analyses, and to delineate the landform units that compose it. The method integrates primary field observation with secondary interpretation of the National Digital Elevation Model (DEMNas), and the landform units were delineated using established genetic landform-classification schemes. The results show that the area is dominated by hills (about 70%), with elevations ranging from 185.49 to 873.29 m and slopes spanning flat (0–2%) to very steep (56–140%). Two main drainage patterns developed: subdendritic (62%) and dendritic (38%), while debris flow and debris slide are the observed mass movements. Based on the integration of these parameters, eleven landform units were identified, ranging from fluvial plains to denudational, karst, and intrusive hills. These units demonstrate that the landscape evolution of the study area is controlled by the combination of lithology, tectonic activity, and exogenic processes of weathering and erosion.

papers.title: Level of awareness and practices of the barangay officials towards disaster risk reduction and management in San Vicente, Palawan, Philippines
papers.summary: Barangay officials have a significant role in local disaster management in the Philippines, where natural hazards such as typhoons frequently occur. This study assessed the level of awareness and practices of barangay officials towards disaster risk reduction and management (DRRM). A descriptive-correlational research design was employed using a structured questionnaire. Gathered data from a total of 75 barangay officials in San Vicente, Palawan were analyzed using descriptive statistics and correlation tests. The results found that most of the respondents are male 53%, with ages between 39-48 years old, have attained college level education, a long-term resident of San Vicente, and had more than six years in government service. The respondents have identified typhoons, flooding, and landslides as the most common disasters experienced within the municipality. Results also revealed that the barangay officials showed high awareness particularly in search and rescue operations, their roles in DRRM, and designated evacuation centers. They also showed regular participation in DRRM activities, specifically training on first aid, search and rescue, and disaster management and information dissemination. However, they identified lack of training, lack of funds, and low community participation as the primary challenges to DRRM implementation. Moreover, results showed that there was no significant correlation between demographic profile and awareness, but disaster experience and DRRM practices did. These findings suggest that prior disaster experiences increase awareness, which in turn increases DRRM involvement. Though, barangay-level DRRM implementation necessitate institutional, financial, and participatory improvements.

papers.title: Kinematic Analysis of the Slopes of the Mutirão Quarry, in Seropédica, Rio de Janeiro, Brazil
papers.summary: Kinematic analysis is one of the methods employed in rock mass stability studies. A detailed analysis was conducted on the slopes of Mutirão Quarry, a decommissioned unit in Seropédica, Rio de Janeiro. The site is used as a “training outcrop” for practical training of geology students at the UFRRJ – Universidade Federal Rural do Rio de Janeiro. The rock mass consists of Neoproterozoic orthogneisses with low-angle dip banding, which does not influence slope stability. For this study, 204 discontinuity measurements collected between 2023 and 2025 were used, and ten slope segments were defined and analyzed, and the results were compared to field observations for validation. Structural analysis indicated four main discontinuity families, and kinematic analysis indicated higher probability of planar sliding and toppling (flexural and direct). However, the analysis revealed a significant discrepancy in wedge failure assessment; the software indicated significant failure probability percentages that were not confirmed in the field. This occurs because the last version of the program does not apply lateral limits to wedges, treating laterally limited planar failures as if they were actual wedges. However, for other processes, the analysis showed high adherence to observed reality.

papers.title: Machine Learning and Explainable AI for Slope Stability Assessment: A Systematic Review of Methods, Parameters, and Research Gaps
papers.source: International Scientific Journal of Engineering and Management
papers.summary: Machine learning (ML) is increasingly used to predict the factor of safety (FoS) and stability state of slopes, often combined with explainable artificial intelligence (XAI). This PRISMA 2020 systematic review searched OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar and Crossref (2000–2026), screened 6,550 unique records, mapped 1,009 eligible studies at abstract level and synthesised 137 open-access full texts. Publications grew sharply after 2020, and artificial neural networks are giving way to tree ensembles, deep learning and metaheuristic hybrids. Reported performance is high (median test 2 0.97; median accuracy 0.93) but rests mainly on synthetic limit-equilibrium or finite-element data (51 % of studies) or on small, overlapping compilations of published case histories (median 190 cases). Only 11 % of studies addressed data quality or duplicates, 39 % used cross-validation, 4 % validated on independent cases and 15 % shared code or data. Class thresholds ranged from FoS 1.0 to 1.3. About half of the studies reported explanations, mostly feature importance, sensitivity analysis or SHAP, but none validated them quantitatively against limit-equilibrium sensitivities. Priorities are curated public datasets, leakage-aware and external validation, explicit target definitions, uncertainty quantification and mechanics-based validation of explanations. Key Words: slope stability, factor of safety, machine learning, explainable artificial intelligence, systematic review, PRISMA

papers.title: Greenfield Finite Element Modelling for Damage Assessment of Axially Rigid Buildings Under Groundwater-Driven Slope Movements
papers.summary: This study presents the results of a numerical analysis aimed to investigate the ground movements induced by groundwater table rise in drained soil conditions on slopes and the deformation patterns associated with axially rigid, shallow-founded buildings located along the slope for a preliminary assessment of the potential induced damage. Slope geometry is examined using a multi-step elastoplastic finite element approach. The numerical simulations reproduce progressive groundwater rise, generating incremental greenfield displacements and strains with the progressive reduction of the factor of safety. The deformation parameters are quantified through greenfield displacements and strains evaluated at different positions along the slope. Damage categories (e.g., slight, moderate, severe) are inferred by correlating computed deformation parameters with established limiting-strain thresholds consistent with an axially rigid structural model. Results demonstrate that increasing pore water pressures significantly amplifies ground displacements whereas the spatial distribution of damage-related strains is primarily controlled by the evolving kinematics of the slope. The modelled ground displacements indicate a predominantly translational response in the central portion of the slope, combined with finite-slope and rotational components near the crest and toe. These kinematic differences control the spatial distribution of greenfield strain distribution, with the highest values mainly concentrated in the upper part of the slope. The proposed approach should therefore be interpreted as a preliminary greenfield-based assessment of strain levels for idealised axially rigid, shallow-founded buildings, rather than as a direct prediction of observed building damage. The results represent an initial step towards a screening-level framework linking groundwater-induced slope deformation, stability reduction and potential building-related strain levels.

papers.title: Assessment of the ecological status of lake Boyuk Ala Gol based on geographic information systems (Case study of Kalbajar District)
papers.source: Journal of Green Economy and Optimization Research
papers.summary: High-mountain lakes play a crucial role in mitigating climate impacts, regulating water flow, recharging groundwater, and ensuring ecological stability. Mapping their extent and monitoring changes is essential to prevent the loss of these ecosystems. However, research on monitoring high-mountain lakes is limited globally, and the subject has not received sufficient attention. This study utilized Geographic Information Systems (GIS) and remote sensing techniques to analyze changes in the surface area of ​​Boyuk Alagol between 1990 and 2023. The research employed the Shuttle Radar Topography Mission (SRTM) digital elevation model to generate slope and Topographic Wetness Index (TWI) maps, while Landsat 4-5 TM and Landsat 8 satellite imagery were used to calculate the Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) and Normalized Difference Water Index (NDWI), as well as to perform supervised classification for various years. Over the past thirty-three years, the lake lost 2.45% of its total surface area, corresponding to an annual reduction of 3.1 km². Research shows that GIS and remote sensing methods are effective for determining the boundaries, mapping, and assessing the dynamics of lakes and wetlands.

papers.title: Evolution of Shear Zone Materials in a Slowly Deforming Rock Slope: Mechanical Implications for Gámanjunni-3, Northern Norway
papers.summary: Rockslides with basal shear zones often creep with periodic accelerations controlled by shear-zone material properties. These properties influence hydraulic conductivity, residual friction angle, and rate dependence. We present mineralogical, grain-size distribution, and ring-shear data from a shear-band soil at the Gámanjunni-3 rockslide Northern Norway. X-ray diffraction indicates phyllosilicate-rich assemblages (>70 wt.% clay minerals) dominated by illite/mica and illite–vermiculite, with minor illite–smectite. Grain-size distributions at outcrop scale are sandy–gravelly. Ring-shear tests on a representative sample give apparent residual friction angle of ≈19–24° and predominantly rate-strengthening behavior from 0.01 to 2 mm/min, with a tentative drop in apparent friction at 10 mm/min. These results are consistent with a model in which deformation localizes along inherited foliation-parallel ductile shear zones, with comminution-driven clay enrichment reducing frictional strength and leading to steady deformation without rapid acceleration periods (the precursor to failure). Gámanjunni-3 is sensitive to external forcing, with implications for seasonal acceleration and climate-driven changes in slope stability in an area where increased rainfall intensity and duration is expected.

papers.title: Influence of Giant-Particle Content on Reservoir-Induced Deformation of Soil–Rock Mixed Bank Slopes: A Physical Simulation Study
papers.summary: Periodic reservoir water level fluctuations significantly affect the stability of soil–rock mixed bank slopes. To investigate the influence of giant-particle content on bank slope deformation during impoundment, physical model tests were conducted using the Zhugangshan Tunnel accumulation body in Tianquan County, Ya'an, as a prototype. Three slope models with different giant-particle contents (10%, 30%, and 50%) were tested under cyclic reservoir water level fluctuations. The results demonstrate that slope deformation mainly occurs during the first impoundment cycle. The deformation process includes soil softening, consolidation settlement, internal erosion, particle loss, and shallow surface sliding. As giant-particle content increases, the heterogeneity of the soil–rock mixture initially weakens slope stability. However, when a stable giant-particle skeleton forms, deformation resistance and overall stability improve significantly. The findings provide a reference for stability assessment and treatment of giant-particle soil–rock bank slopes in reservoir areas.

papers.title: Static Versus Dynamic Elastic Moduli in Gneiss: A Comparative Study for Geotechnical Characterization
papers.summary: This study aimed to compare analysis of elastic modulus values obtained using dynamic (Ed) and static (Est) methods on four gneiss samples to assess the applicability of non-destructive techniques for geotechnical applications, such as slope stability analysis in mining operations. The dynamic methods employed were the Impulse Excitation Technique (IET) and the Ultrasonic Pulse Velocity (UPV), while static reference values were obtained from uniaxial compressive strength (UCS) tests. Physical index tests (density and porosity) were also performed. The results indicated that the dynamic moduli were consistently higher than those obtained from UCS tests. The UPV-derived dynamic modulus (EdUPV) was on average 18% higher than dynamic modulus fram IET (EdIET). The static modulus estimated from IET (EstIET) showed the closest agreement with EstUCS, being only 12% higher on average. The sample with the lowest porosity and highest density exhibited the greatest stiffness. The IET method provided estimates that were reasonably close to the reference static elastic modulus obtained from UCS testing, offering a rapid, non-destructive alternative for field applications. The findings contribute to the optimization of geotechnical investigations in challenging environments.

papers.title: Efficient Finite Element Modeling of Initial K0 Geostress and Shear-Slide Stability in Sloping Ground
papers.summary: Abstract Reliable initialization of in situ $${K}_{0}$$ K 0 stresses and efficient stability analysis are fundamental to robust finite-element modeling of infinite slopes. Yet, existing modeling schemes either apply gravity loading with an indirect $${K}_{0}-\nu $$ K 0 - ν mapping that is not mechanics-consistent for sloping ground, or require large computational domains that are expensive for repeated analyses. In this study, an efficient FEM framework is developed that retains the gravity load procedure (GLP) and addresses its stress-initialization limitation for homogeneous infinite slopes. Specifically, a closed-form coupling of Poisson’s ratio components is derived within a transversely isotropic elastic formulation, in which slope cross-anisotropy arises from stress-induced anisotropy. This coupling enforces target $${K}_{0}$$ K 0 -type geostress states in sloping ground, without using the conventional horizontal-ground $${K}_{0}-\nu $$ K 0 - ν relation. The formulation is implemented in a compact periodic unit-block FEM model (Geometry I, L/H = 0.2). It is combined with strength-reduction using an elastic–perfectly plastic Mohr–Coulomb model for shear-slide factor-of-safety (FOS) assessment. Results are evaluated against analytical infinite-slope solutions and conventional large-domain FEM simulations (Geometry II, L/H = 32) performed using COMSOL Multiphysics and PLAXIS 2D. The proposed model reproduces analytical $${K}_{0}$$ K 0 stress profiles across tested slope angles and pore-pressure ratios. It avoids spurious yielding during geostress initialization and provides FOS predictions in close agreement with analytical solutions under both dry and seepage-parallel conditions. Compared with the large-domain approach, it delivers substantially improved efficiency (at least ~ 4 × shorter runtime in tested cases) with orders-of-magnitude fewer degrees of freedom, while preserving the expected slope-parallel failure mechanism. The effects of slope angle, pore-pre

papers.title: Recent Experiences with the Slope Stability Probability Classification (SSPC)
papers.summary: The Slope Stability Probability Classification (SSPC) is a classification system designed for estimating stability of slopes. The classification system is based on probabilities for individual failure mechanisms acting in slopes. Failure mechanisms considered are sliding, plane and wedge sliding, toppling, and groundmass failure. The SSPC works with weighting factors for method of excavation and weathering to compensate for past and future damage and changes due to method of excavation and weathering. The SSPC system may forecast major slides or failure of masses but also includes smaller but still devastating effects on the stability of a slope, such as loss of structure, raveling, and erosion of a slope. The SSPC system was developed on mainly rock slopes but also works for groundmasses with a more soil-type character. The system was developed in the early 1990’s and has been used throughout the world since thereafter. Some of the slopes that were classified in the 1990’s have been revisited in recent years to see whether the SSPC system still holds. In addition, a couple of other slopes have been assessed. The slopes are located in the Falset region in Catalunya, Spain, and in Germany. The results show the SSPC system is still very much useful and forecasts stability to a high degree of reliability.

papers.title: Concrete Over-Consumption in Non-Displacement Piles in Dikes Due to Concrete Pressure
papers.summary: In dike reinforcement projects in the Netherlands, non-displacement pile walls are frequently used to enhance slope stability while minimizing disruption to nearby infrastructure. However, when installed in soft soil conditions such as clay or peat, these piles often exhibit concrete over-consumption. This phenomenon is partly attributed to the lateral pressure exerted by fresh concrete on the surrounding soil, which may deform the borehole and increase the required concrete volume. Despite its practical relevance, this mechanism remains underexplored in current design practice. This study investigates the impact of concrete pressure on soil deformation and over-consumption during pile installation. Using three-dimensional finite element models, compared to data from the Lekdijk reinforcement project, we simulate borehole deformation across various soil profiles and concrete pouring rates. Results show that in soft soils, rapid concreting can induce significant horizontal deformation, up to 10 cm at the dike toe, and lead to concrete over-consumption exceeding 25%. In contrast, stiffer soils such as silty and clayey layers reduce both deformation and material excess, often keeping over-consumption below 10%. Furthermore, while reducing the concrete pouring rate can mitigate deformation, it may result in early setting of the concrete before casing extraction is completed, potentially forming vertical gaps that compromise hydraulic integrity. These findings highlight the need to optimize pouring rates based on subsoil conditions, balancing construction efficiency, cost, and dike stability.

papers.title: Effects of Root–Crack Dynamics on Soil Infiltration During the Growth Period Across Seasons
papers.summary: Reliable measurement of soil infiltration is fundamental in geotechnical engineering, especially when evaluating slope stability. Although vegetation is widely recognised for enhancing environmental resilience, the impact of plant roots on soil permeability remains debated in the literature. In addition, desiccation cracks play a critical role in modifying infiltration behaviour, particularly under seasonal changes. This study explores the coupled effects of root development and crack formation on infiltration rates across different seasons. Infiltration rates were measured directly in both bare and vegetated plots over a six-month observation period using the double-ring infiltrometer method. The interaction mechanisms between root development and crack dynamics were quantified through the Root Area Ratio (RAR) and Crack Identification Factor (CIF), assessed using a minirhizotron imaging system. The results demonstrate that as vetiver roots developed, they substantially altered crack characteristics, reducing 2 times lower CIF and producing a more irregular crack network compared to bare soil. Statistical analysis revealed positive correlations between both RAR and CIF with infiltration rate, suggesting that root proliferation and crack presence jointly facilitate water entry into the soil. Compared with the bare zone, the vegetated area exhibited markedly higher final infiltration rates, approximately 2.7 times greater in the summer dry period. The results indicate that infiltration was controlled by both surface cracking and vegetation-induced soil structure. Although bare soil exhibited higher CIF, vegetated plots showed higher infiltration rates, particularly during the dry summer period. This suggests that root-induced macropores and improved pore connectivity enhanced infiltration independently of visible surface crack.

papers.title: Mechanical and Microstructural Characterization of Deformed Volcaniclastic Rocks from the Lower Comondú, Baja California Sur, Mexico
papers.summary: Volcaniclastic rocks are widespread in tectonically deformed regions and play a key role in slope stability and hazard mitigation. However, their mechanical behavior remains poorly understood, particularly in weakly lithified, porous rock masses. This study examines the deformation mechanisms of pyroclastic and volcanoclastic rocks of the Lower Comondú Group in southern Baja California, Mexico. Field mapping reveals Miocene compressional deformation, characterized by folding, faulting, and injection features related to crustal shortening. Uniaxial and triaxial compressive tests were conducted on rock specimens. Unconfined and confined tests (30 MPa) were performed using a servo-hydraulic MTS 815 system with cyclic loading protocols. In addition, micro-CT scans were performed before and after these mechanical tests to monitor microstructural changes. Ignimbrites samples exhibit unconfined compressive strength (UCS) values of 16.5–17.5 MPa and elastic moduli of 0.8– 1 GPa, while sandstones range from 13.2 to 18.8 MPa and 0.78–1.6 GPa, respectively. Poisson’s ratios range from 0.1 to 0.3. The results indicate that porosity, mineralogy, and pumice-rich textures strongly control the brittle–ductile transition. Cyclic loading experiments also reveal progressive fracture development, stiffness degradation, and dilatancy. Micro-CT image analysis confirms that the internal damage zones are aligned with fractures existing in the non-deformed specimen. These results improve the geomechanical characterization of volcanosedimentary successions in compressive tectonic settings relevant for slope stability analysis, engineering design, and the assessment of geohazards in volcanic terrains such as those in some places in Baja California, México.

papers.title: Numerical Integration and Step-Size Sensitivity for a Coupled Hydro-Mechanical Constitutive Model of Root-Reinforced Unsaturated Soil
papers.summary: Increasing rainfall variability driven by climate change poses growing challenges to the stability of unsaturated slopes, where hydraulic and mechanical processes are highly coupled. Vegetation provides an effective nature-based solution, but its integration into quantitative geomechanical models remains limited. This study builds on a coupled hydro-mechanical constitutive model that incorporates root reinforcement effects within unsaturated soils. The formulation extends the Barcelona Basic Model by introducing root volume fraction as an internal variable, which modifies the critical state parameter, preconsolidation stress, and shear strength evolution. Both suction and biological reinforcement are treated as independent state variables that govern the yield surface geometry, hardening behaviour, and deformation response under environmental loading. The model is implemented using an implicit elastic predictor–plastic corrector stress update under strain control, and the numerical integration accuracy is evaluated through a step-size sensitivity study. Numerical results demonstrate convergence of the deviatoric and volumetric responses to a fine-increment benchmark and quantify relative errors as a function of strain increment. These findings provide practical guidance for selecting strain increments in subsequent parametric and finite-element simulations, where suction evolution and root-volume effects are activated and numerical artefacts must be distinguished from physical trends.

papers.title: Engineering Geology and Asset Management of 3000 km of Track Embankment
papers.summary: ProRail, the Dutch infrastructural manager of 7,000 km track on ~3,000 km of railway embankments, initiated a project focussed on railway embankment stability. Although most of these embankments were constructed over a hundred years ago and still function effectively, recent calculations revealed concerns regarding their stability. To ensure safe future use of the embankments, it has been determined that any modifications to the tracks or embankments must be preceded by thorough investigations. At the start of the project in 2020, predictions were made regarding increased future usage of the Dutch railway tracks. Combined with the impacts of climate change, this led ProRail to recognise the necessity of gaining a better understanding of railway embankment stability. Unfortunately, the available information regarding the subsurface and embankments was limited, demanding a novel approach to investigate all embankment slopes in a cost-effective way. Therefore, the Stochastic Subsoil Schematisation (SSS) approach was deployed for characterising and parameterising embankment composition and natural subsurface. This approach was combined with an automated workflow to assess slope stability.In the Netherlands, a wide range of geospatial data is available such as geological maps, ground elevation information, Cone Penetration Test data, borehole records and groundwater table measurements. This data served as the foundation for the SSS-procedure. Multiple subsoil scenarios were developed per segment, with stability calculations for each embankment slope conducted in D-Stability and automated using Python. With this, the stability of the ~3,000 km of railway embankment could be estimated, and the results were visualised in Geographic Information System (GIS) for clear presentation.

papers.title: Processed monitoring and calculation-audit data for identifiability and consistency analysis of weak deformation signals in long-term high-slope monitoring
papers.summary: This dataset supports the article “Identifiability and consistency of weak deformation signals in long-term high-slope monitoring”. It contains processed point-level and interval-level monitoring records, analysis-window classifications, figure source data and calculation-audit records used to evaluate whether weak deformation signals are identifiable and internally consistent under explicitly declared criteria. The dataset includes a consolidated analysis workbook (Evidence_Matrix.xlsx), interval-level analysis-window classifications, point-level records for the uniquely identified primary vertical interval, and the source data used for Figures 1–4. It also includes a README file describing the provenance fields, variable definitions, units, missing-value codes, audit-status categories and figure-to-file mappings. The data were derived from engineering monitoring reports for the BX30–BX55 high slope. Record-level provenance includes the report period, PDF page, observation date, point identifier, metric, sign convention, original observation text and audit status where available. Verification flags and numerical inconsistencies retained during the audit are included rather than removed. The original engineering monitoring reports and source PDFs contain third-party project information and are not included in this public record. This dataset is limited to processed analysis records, figure source data and calculation-audit information required to inspect the analyses and figures reported in the article. This record does not infer geomechanical mechanisms, slope stability conditions or future movement. Users should interpret the classifications only under the criteria defined in the associated article and README.

papers.title: Integration of 3D Technology in Rock Slope Classification: A New Era
papers.summary: Traditional rock mass classification systems, such as the Rock Mass Rating (RMR) and the Slope Mass Rating (SMR), rely on empirical parameters derived from field observations, including rock strength, RQD, spacing and condition of discontinuities, groundwater conditions, and geometric relationships between joints and slope faces. These systems have long served as essential tools for assessing slope stability and remain central to engineering geology practice. However, their accuracy often depends on subjective field observations and limited spatial coverage. The integration of 3D point cloud technology, acquired through LiDAR or structure-from-motion techniques, offers a paradigm shift in how rock slopes are characterized. High-resolution 3D models enable the extraction of structural and morphological features, allow objective identification and discrimination of rock, soil, and mixed units, and provide accurate quantification of slope geometry and discontinuity patterns, which are used in empirical classification systems. This study presents a web-based, open-source framework that integrates high-resolution 3D point cloud data with automated segmentation and machine learning for rock slope classification and hazard assessment. By embedding traditional rock mass classification systems within a scalable, 3D-driven digital environment, the proposed framework aims to enhance the precision, repeatability, and transparency of slope stability and rockfall hazard assessment. Integrating 3D technology marks a significant step toward a more robust, data-driven approach for assessing slope stability and informing geotechnical design, marking the beginning of a new era in rock mass classification.

papers.title: Drought modulates soil hydraulic, biological, and physicochemical responses to one-off tillage in a long-term cover-cropped Mediterranean vineyard
papers.summary: Sustainable soil management is a crucial factor to maintain soil health and long-term functionality in vineyards. In Mediterranean climates, cover crops have become a sustainable alternative to conventional tillage due to their positive effects on soil structure, water retention, and biological activity. Severe drought episodes are increasingly prompting growers to incorporate tillage to reduce water and nutrient competition between cover crops and grapevines. However, the immediate consequences of this practice on soil attributes remain poorly understood. To evaluate whether reintroducing tillage is a viable short-term strategy to relieve drought-induced water competition without compromising soil health, this study assessed the effects of a single tillage event on soil hydraulic properties (water retention curve, unsaturated hydraulic conductivity, Ku and field-saturated soil hydraulic conductivity, Kfs), physical and chemical properties (bulk density, total porosity, pore size distribution, total organic carbon, pH, CaCO 3 ) and biological properties (dehydrogenase and β-glucosidase activity) in a long-term cover-cropped organic vineyard of Vitis vinifera L. cv. Cabernet Sauvignon in Raïmat (Lleida, Spain), under commercial and survival water regimes. Soil water content dynamics were monitored, focusing on the April-June period when cover crop competition for water is greatest. Tillage reduced bulk density by 4.3% (1.35 ± 0.01 vs. 1.41 ± 0.02 g cm −3 , p = 0.020) and increased total porosity by 6.5% (0.49 ± 0.01 vs. 0.46 ± 0.01, p = 0.029) relative to cover crop, with no significant differences at field capacity (p = 0.352) or permanent wilting point (p = 0.264). Kfs was significantly higher under tillage regardless of water regime. Neither dehydrogenase nor β-glucosidase activity showed a significant reduction under tillage, suggesting that the measured biological indicators were not compromised by the one-off disturbance. papers.title: Impact of the spatial layout of effective impervious area increments on urban stormwater peak flow and runoff volume
papers.source: DOAJ (DOAJ: Directory of Open Access Journals)
papers.summary: To reveal the influence mechanism of the layout of effective impervious area (EIA) on urban stormwater processes，a refined stormwater model was constructed，and upstream and downstream sub-catchments were delineated. Taking the Shuangqiaobang runoff plot in Changzhou，Southern Jiangsu，China，as a typical study area，the impact on peak flow and runoff volume were systematically analyzed by setting different scenarios of EIA increments with different locations and scales. Results showed that the location of the EIA，infiltration capacity of the original pervious surface，and rainfall magnitude are key factors affecting the hydrological response. The spatial location effect of newly added EIA is significant，with the growth rates of peak flow and runoff volume in downstream areas being significantly higher than those in upstream areas，showing maximum difference of 18.48% and 7.70% under the moderate-infiltration scenario，respectively. Pervious areas with stronger original infiltration capacity exhibit a greater proportional increase in runoff after conversion to EIA. The growth rates of peak flow and runoff volume tend to decrease with increasing rainfall return period，exhibiting an amplification effect under low-return-period rainfall events. This study provides a scientific basis for optimizing the spatial patterns of underlying surfaces in urban settings and guiding the rational layout of stormwater facilities.

papers.title: Assessment of Fully Polarimetric Biomass Data for Soil Moisture Retrieval
papers.summary: Water management for irrigation is an essential activity especially in agricultural areas or where water is scarce. Water storage in the soil affects the vapour transpiration but also its heat storage capacity, its thermal conductivity and the energy separation between latent and sensible heat fluxes. From a hydrological perspective, soil moisture links the partitioning of rainfall into runoff and infiltration and therefore it has an important role in several ecological applications as flood forecasting, crop yield expectation, meteorological prediction, erosion and slope failure forecasting, water reservoir management, etc. Most of the soil moisture models describe only the bare soil response. In a real scenario, the presence of bare soil is not common as most of the time some kind of vegetation may be found on top. In order to reduce the amount of vegetation responses in addition to the soil moisture estimation longer wavelength can be used. In this study we like to explore the polarimetric and interferometric response of the BIOMASS mission, which operates in P band wavelength. Polarimetry can be used to define the scattering mechanisms and is able, when using decomposition methods to separate the ground and vegetation contribution. To perform this separation a physical model is employed and fully polarimetric data is needed in order to invert for the different involved parameters. It is worth mentioning that for extracting the ground response and the corresponding soil moisture, a significant degree of penetration into vegetation is required. For this reason, SAR soil moisture inversion has traditionally been investigated with L-band. In this study we use quad polarimetry in P band to investigate the sensitivity to bare soil and vegetated soil for soil moisture estimation [R1]. Differential SAR interferometry, a popular technique for measuring displacements of the Earth's surface, is potentially influenced by changes in soil moisture. Different mechanisms for th

papers.title: Field Hydraulic Conductivity Test in Clayey Soils: Evaluation Aquifer Recharge Challenges
papers.summary: Climate change is altering rainfall patterns, leading to greater intensity and shorter duration of events. This generates significant surface runoff, causes flooding, and decreases natural aquifer recharge. Consequently, methods for artificial aquifer recharge must be evaluated, as groundwater extraction continues while natural infiltration declines. Baseline conditions must be investigated to evaluate phreatic levels, recharge areas, hydrogeochemistry, and isotopes, among other parameters. In Uruguay, the Raigón Aquifer is a vital groundwater resource utilized for agricultural and industrial activities, as well as drinking water. The Libertad Clay, an aquitard composed of clayey and silty-clayey soils, overlies the Raigón Aquifer. Regional piezometric levels indicate that recharge occurs through the Libertad Clay where its thickness ranges between 20 m and 35 m. In this study, field and laboratory tests were conducted to measure the hydraulic conductivity (HC) of the Libertad Clay and determined whether recharge through this aquitard is viable. In the field, 3 m deep wells were constructed for infiltration testing, and soil samples were collected every 0.5 m for laboratory classification and HC testing. Laboratory HC values were lower than 10-9 m/s, whereas field infiltration rates ranged from 10-6 m/s to 10-7 m/s. As a result, field infiltration rates were 100 to 1,000 times higher than laboratory measurements, finding that field testing provides a more representative evaluation of the hydraulic behavior of the Libertad Clay for aquifer recharge. Ongoing complementary research aims to identify the specific processes driving this recharge to inform future managed aquifer recharge strategies.

papers.title: Laboratory evaluation of capillary rise in silty sands with geotextile
papers.summary: Capillary rise of water in soil from a groundwater table is commonly observed in soils with fines. The capillary rise increases moisture in subgrade and base course with fines, thus affecting roadway performance. Fines content controls the level of capillary rise and geotextile may affect this level. Limited research has quantitatively evaluated capillary rise in unsaturated soils considering the influence of soil fines content and geotextiles. This paper presents a laboratory study evaluating capillary rise in silty sands with varying fines contents and the effects of wicking and non-wicking geotextiles. Soil columns consisting of upper and lower boxes were placed in a water tub to allow capillary rise, and volumetric moisture contents were monitored using moisture sensors over a 14-day period. At the end of each test, gravimetric moisture contents were measured to establish their relationship with the volumetric moisture contents. The test results indicate that capillary rise increased with the fines content. Existing methods were found to either under- or overestimate capillary rise in sands with fines. Non-wicking geotextiles acted as capillary barriers, restricting upward moisture migration above the interface, whereas wicking geotextiles were less effective in limiting upward capillary movement but enhanced horizontal drainage. Soil Water Characteristics Curves (SWCCs) and relative Hydraulic Conductivity Functions (HCFs) were also estimated and compared with the literature-based Geotextile Water Characteristics Curves (GWCCs). Analysis indicated that the non-wicking geotextile created a hydraulic discontinuity that reduced and delayed upward capillary water movement, particularly in soils with higher fines contents.

papers.title: Grass Pavers
papers.source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.summary: Grass pavers provide a reliable way to strengthen lawn areas while preserving their natural appearance. Rather than installing concrete or relying on loose gravel that can shift, wash away, or develop ruts, these interlocking grids create a supportive foundation beneath the grass. Their open-cell design allows roots to grow naturally while the durable structure distributes weight across the surface. Our 24" x 24" permeable pavers are manufactured from recycled high-density plastic and feature an 87% porosity rating. This design allows rainwater to pass through the panels and soak into the ground, helping reduce standing water, muddy patches, and soil erosion. Each lightweight panel covers 4 square feet and weighs only 3.2 pounds. The convenient loop-to-peg connection system makes installation straightforward, allowing many homeowners to complete projects such as driveway extensions and additional parking spaces over a weekend.

papers.title: Dataset and R Code for "Biochar Increases Penetration Resistance Despite Acidity Relief and Greater Soil Moisture in Hardsetting Soils"
